translation_en:
…If there is further concern that present resources are insufficient, then the practice under our imperial ancestors of admitting men to the Imperial University in return for contributions of grain or horses could temporarily be put into effect. Finances are exhausted by the multitude of troops, and strength is dispersed among too many defensive positions. Eliminating redundant personnel and concentrating defenses could also somewhat reduce expenditure. The salt administration and military agricultural colonies, however, must without fail be restored in due sequence. A scholar living in a humble thatched dwelling cannot adequately comprehend the great plans of the realm; yet, since your illuminating question touches on these matters, how could I dare not exhaust my meager understanding? As for devoting every effort to thorough deliberation and resolutely seeking a reversal of our fortunes, thereby helping our Emperor achieve a government that follows his ancestors and safeguards the state: this is assuredly the responsibility of the court’s highest ministers. Respectfully submitted in reply.

He Tang 何鏜

If your proposals are implemented, security for ten thousand generations will thereby be established enduringly.

…such people, then—how much more so the children of their native land? This is the second essential point.
Counterspies are enemy spies whom one turns to one’s own use. When enemy spies come to spy upon us, we guide them with the prospect of gain and release them; thus counterspies can be obtained and employed. Yet today some tighten the orders for apprehending spies while abandoning the art of employing them. This deprives the armies of what they depend upon. The five kinds of spies have been the means by which famous generals achieved success since antiquity. This is the third essential point.
Today, customs grow more debased by the day, especially in the frontier regions. When a husband dies, someone else takes possession of his wife; when a father dies, someone else takes possession of his children. If a father cannot protect his children and a husband cannot protect his wife, how can the state command the service of its people? This is why the sense of duty to cherish one’s superiors and die for one’s leaders is fading away. Truly encourage integrity and a sense of shame, and cultivate moral instruction, so that the people’s spirit of loyalty and righteousness binds them firmly together without dissolving. It was through this that Zhang Xun inspired the bloody fighting at Suiyang, and Yue Fei secretly united the loyal and righteous men of the Two Rivers region to restore the Song ruling house. This is the fourth essential point.
When a general is with his army, there are commands from the ruler that he does not accept. Military affairs cannot be assessed from afar, nor can discretionary authority be controlled from the court. Today, however, generals are hampered by deadlines and rendezvous, checked by discouraging words, and weakened into timidity as they hesitate between compliance and resistance. If this is so, the general’s orders will not be carried out and his soldiers will not obey commands. How, then, can success be demanded of him? Authority to act as circumstances require must therefore not be abolished. This is the fifth essential point.

天命首令天下設文武科取士用
集大業文明之運所由啓矣
宣德成化之際仁義融液王
道明洽人文之化日益宣著
至于今
聖天子懋至德配天地稽古三五
===
之道勸學修禮崇教厲賢以
風四方海內懽慕含和咀淳
天符人瑞雜然並至
神光曜暉洪洞朗天豈不明盛之
極哉士生其時固宜皆林林
成有滋味也然萬物養于天
地而人則藉萬物以養也物
punctuated: 高皇帝肇受天命，首令天下設文武科取士，用集大業，文明之運所由啓矣。宣德、成化之際，仁義融液，王道明洽，人文之化日益宣著。至于今，聖天子懋至德，配天地，稽古三五之道，勸學修禮，崇教勵賢，以風四方。海內懽慕，含和咀淳，天符人瑞雜然並至。神光曜暉，洪洞朗天，豈不明盛之極哉！士生其時，固宜皆彬彬成有滋味也。然萬物養于天地，而人則籍萬物以養也。物
translation_en: … Emperor Gao first received Heaven’s Mandate and at the outset ordered the establishment of civil and military examinations throughout the realm to select men for service, thereby bringing his great undertaking to fruition. Thus began an era of cultural brilliance. During the Xuande and Chenghua reigns, benevolence and righteousness permeated all; the Kingly Way shone forth and spread everywhere, and the transforming influence of culture became more manifest each day. Now the sagely Son of Heaven cultivates consummate virtue, matching Heaven and Earth. He studies the ancient Way of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, encourages learning and the observance of ritual, honors instruction, and spurs on the worthy, thereby influencing the four quarters. All within the seas rejoice in admiration, imbibing harmony and savoring purity. Heavenly signs and auspicious manifestations among humankind arrive together in profusion. Divine radiance shines forth, vast and pervasive, illuminating the heavens. Is this not the very height of brilliant flourishing? Scholars born in such an age should surely all attain a harmonious balance of refinement and substance, maturing and acquiring savor. Yet the myriad things are nourished by Heaven and Earth, while human beings rely upon the myriad things for their nourishment. Things …

title: 嘉靖二十六年會試錄
text:
味有美惡斯生理之肥瘠因
之矣荼堇烏喙螫吻酸鼻决
腸胃而毒者則人避而棄之
敗粃之稊無捄饑渴封熊之
趾豢豹之胎窮海逾陸非可
常有亦人所不尚也何者以
無藉於養也士者人君所與
===
共成養萬民也士味有厚薄
而世治盛衰恒所由之
國初之士其味眞實茂以開濟
之畧翊戴休烈當時之民無
不得其養者宣成熙盈之運
士多持重完固其味醇厚民
得所養者則皆充然而肥有

共成養萬民也士味有厚薄
而世治盛衰恒所由之
國初之士其味真實茂以閎濟
之畧翊戴休烈當時之民無
不得其養者宣成熙盈之運
士多持重完固其味醇厚民
得所養者則皆充然而肥有
punctuated:
味有美惡，斯生理之肥瘠因之矣。荼堇烏喙，螫吻酸鼻，决腸胃而毒者，則人避而棄之。敗粃之稊，無捄饑渴；封熊之趾，豢豹之胎，窮海逾陸，非可常有，亦人所不尚也。何者？以無藉於養也。士者，人君所與共成養萬民也。士味有厚薄，而世治盛衰恒所由之。

translation_en:
…flavors may be good or bad, and whether life is well nourished or impoverished depends upon them. Bitter herbs, poisonous violets, and aconite sting the lips, irritate the nose, and rend the stomach and intestines with their poison; people therefore avoid and discard them. Spoiled, empty grain and darnel [?] do nothing to relieve hunger or thirst. The paws of great bears and the fetuses of fattened leopards, sought to the ends of the seas and across the land, cannot be regularly available; these too are things people do not prize. Why? Because they cannot be relied upon for nourishment. Scholars are those with whom the ruler jointly accomplishes the nourishment of the myriad people. Whether scholars possess a rich or insipid flavor is a constant determinant of the flourishing or decline of government in their age.
The scholars of the dynasty’s founding had a true and substantial flavor. Abounding in strategies for establishing order and bringing affairs to fruition, they supported its glorious achievements, and none of the people of that time failed to receive nourishment. During the flourishing and abundant reigns of Xuande and Chenghua, scholars were mostly circumspect, steadfast, and sound; their flavor was mellow and rich. The people who received their nourishment were all amply filled and well fed, possessing…

title: 嘉靖二十六年會試錄
text:
光澤也及久而變焉譬之禁
羞珍臠漸以蜜醴和以椒桂
芬馨有餘而真味或薄矣其
養之惠於天下者視在昔何
如哉乃下焉者伐德暴義回
惑營蠱惟淫志是逞用導民
亂荼堇烏喙螫吻酸鼻决腸
===
胃而毒者也委瑣頹靡饕貴
利自富于民弗勤敗粃之粻
無捄饑渴也幽竒詭激違衆
立異以改易觀聽民日漸於
匪彝封熊之趾豢豹之胎窮
海逾陸非所常有也數者於
養之理何述哉民生日彫瘁
alt_text:
光澤也及久而變焉譬之禁
羞珍爨漸以蜜醴和以椒桂
芬馨有餘而眞味或薄矣其
養之惠於天下者視在昔何
如哉乃下焉者伐鶴棊義回
惑營蠱惟淫志是逞用導民
亂荼堇烏喙鴆啄酸鼻决腸
===
胃而毒者也委瑣頹靡饕餮貴
利自富于民弗勤敗粃之糈
無擇饑渴也幽奇詭激違衆
立異以改易觀聽民用漸於
匪彝封熊之趾豢豹之胎窮
海逾陸非所常有也數者於
養之理何述哉民生日彫瘁
punctuated: 光澤也。及久而變焉，譬之禁羞珍臠，漸以蜜醴，和以椒桂，芬馨有餘而真味或薄矣。其養之惠於天下者，視在昔何如哉？乃下焉者，伐德暴義，回惑營蠱，惟淫志是逞，用導民亂，荼堇烏喙，螫吻酸鼻，决腸胃而毒者也。委瑣頹靡，饕貴利，自富于民弗勤，敗粃之粻，無捄饑渴也。幽竒詭激，違衆立異，以改易觀聽，民日漸於匪彝，封熊之趾，豢豹之胎，窮海逾陸，非所常有也。數者於養之理何述哉？民生日彫瘁
translation_en:
…and lustrous. As time passed, however, a change occurred. It was like rare delicacies from the imperial kitchen, steeped in honey and sweet wine and seasoned with pepper and cinnamon: their fragrance was abundant, but their true flavor had perhaps grown thin. How did the benefits their nourishment brought to all under Heaven compare with those of former times?

Those of a still lower sort assail virtue and violate righteousness, deceive and sow corruption, and seek only to gratify their unbridled desires, thereby leading the people into disorder. They are like bitter herbs and aconite: they sting the lips, irritate the nose, and poison by rending the stomach and bowels. Petty and dispirited, greedy for high status and profit, they enrich themselves but exert no effort for the people. They are spoiled, chaff-filled provisions, offering no relief from hunger or thirst. Others cultivate obscurity, oddity, perversity, and extremism, opposing the multitude and setting themselves apart to alter what people see and hear, while the people are daily steeped in what violates proper norms. These are like the paws of great bears and the fetuses of captive-reared leopards: things sought to the ends of the seas and across the land, not ordinarily available. What merit can these several kinds claim in the principles of nourishment? The people's livelihood daily withers and declines…

title: 嘉靖二十六年會試錄
text:
若抱瘡瘵而懼其斃焉夫豈
氣化使然耶要亦養之道未
至耳是故養生者必擇味養
民者必擇士而士之自養者
必擇道今夫
國家之擇士也三歲比天下之
士而鄉試之三歲比其鄉之
===
士而會試之其法至備也及
加之民乃無藉於養焉豈非
以人之難知而言之不可以
稽乎稂莠之始夭然與嘉穀
並茂而其味則遠矣故擇不
可以不慎也然士之自擇亦
猶國之擇士也國之擇士也

===
加之民乃無藉於養焉豈非
以人之難知而言之不可以
稽乎稂莠之始夭然與嘉穀
並茂而其味則遠矣故擇不
可以不慎也然士之自擇亦
猶國之擇士也國之擇士也
punctuated: 若抱瘡瘵而懼其斃焉，夫豈氣化使然耶？要亦養之道未至耳。是故養生者必擇味，養民者必擇士，而士之自養者必擇道。今夫國家之擇士也，三歲比天下之士而鄉試之，三歲比其鄉之士而會試之，其法至備也。及加之民，乃無藉於養焉，豈非以人之難知而言之不可以稽乎？稂莠之始，夭然與嘉穀並茂，而其味則遠矣，故擇不可以不慎也。然士之自擇，亦猶國之擇士也。國之擇士也，
translation_en: …as though afflicted with sores and wasting illness, fearing death. Could this really be caused by the transformations of vital energy? In essence, it is simply that the way of nourishing them has not been fully realized. Thus, those who nourish life must choose their food; those who nourish the people must choose their scholars; and scholars who nourish themselves must choose their Way. Now, in selecting scholars, the state every three years assembles the scholars of the realm and examines them in the Provincial Examination; every three years it assembles the scholars from those provinces and examines them in the Metropolitan Examination. Its procedures are thoroughly complete. Yet when those selected are set over the people, the people find no support for their nourishment. Is this not because people are difficult to know and their words cannot be verified? When weeds first sprout, they flourish luxuriantly alongside good grain, yet their flavors differ greatly. Selection must therefore be undertaken with care. But scholars’ choosing for themselves is likewise comparable to the state’s choosing scholars. As for the state’s selection of scholars…

title: 嘉靖二十六年會試錄
text:
蘄以其士之道養乎天下也
夫其士之道誠養乎天下而
後可爲民之味不然其有味
之者乎士之自擇也蘄以其
身之道養乎天下也夫其身
之道誠養乎天下而後可爲
國之味不然其有能味者乎
===
===
是故國以士爲味士以道爲
味而後明盛之理可從致矣
昔者伊尹之於湯也思說以
堯舜之味而高宗之於傅說
亦惟曰爾惟麴糵惟鹽梅斯
二者非所謂天下之至味者
乎商道之盛至今猶耿光者

是故國以士爲味士以道爲
味而後明盛之理可從致矣
昔者伊尹之於湯也思說以
堯舜之味而高宗之於傅說
亦惟曰爾惟麴蘖惟鹽梅斯
二者非所謂天下之至味者
乎商道之盛至今猶耿光者
punctuated: 蘄以其士之道養乎天下也。夫其士之道誠養乎天下，而後可爲民之味；不然，其有味之者乎？士之自擇也，蘄以其身之道養乎天下也。夫其身之道誠養乎天下，而後可爲國之味；不然，其有能味者乎？是故國以士爲味，士以道爲味，而後明盛之理可從致矣。昔者伊尹之於湯也，思說以堯舜之味；而高宗之於傅說，亦惟曰：「爾惟麴糵，惟鹽梅。」斯二者，非所謂天下之至味者乎？商道之盛，至今猶耿光者，
translation_en: …seeks to nourish all under Heaven through the Way of its scholars. Only when the Way of those scholars truly nourishes all under Heaven can it become something for the people to savor. Otherwise, would anyone savor it? In choosing for themselves, scholars seek to nourish all under Heaven through the Way embodied in their own persons. Only when that Way truly nourishes all under Heaven can it become something for the state to savor. Otherwise, could anyone savor it? Thus the state takes scholars as its savor, and scholars take the Way as theirs; only then can enlightened and flourishing governance be achieved. In former times, Yi Yin sought to persuade Tang with the savor of Yao and Shun; and Gaozong likewise said to Fu Yue: “You shall be the yeast and malt, the salt and plums.” Were these two men not what are called the finest flavors in all under Heaven? That the flourishing Way of the Shang still shines brightly to this day…

title: 嘉靖二十六年會試錄
text:
其有以致之矣爾多士以丁
未進其亦慎擇所為味如商
之二臣以惠天下之養以仰
對
聖天子明盛之理則唯亦有聞於
無窮哉臣治不佞辱
詔從大夫之後與校試之責焉敬
===
以是申告之末簡
掌翰林院事通議大夫吏部
左侍郎兼翰林院學士張治
謹序

掌翰林院事通議大夫吏部
左侍郎兼翰林院學士張〔治〕
謹序
punctuated:
其有以致之矣。爾多士以丁未進，其亦慎擇所為味，如商之二臣，以惠天下之養，以仰對聖天子明盛之理，則唯亦有聞於無窮哉！臣治不佞，辱詔從大夫之後，與校試之責焉，敬以是申告之末簡。
掌翰林院事、通議大夫、吏部左侍郎兼翰林院學士張治謹序。
translation_en:
…there were means by which this was brought about. You many scholars who advance in this dingwei year [1547] should likewise carefully choose what you take as your savor, emulating the two ministers of Shang, so as to benefit the nourishment of all under Heaven and respond worthily to the enlightened and flourishing rule of the sagely Son of Heaven. Then surely your renown too will endure forever! Your servant Zhi, though lacking in ability, was honored by an imperial command to follow in the ranks of the high officials and share responsibility for evaluating the examination. I respectfully reiterate this admonition here on the final leaf.
Preface respectfully composed by Zhang Zhi, in charge of the Hanlin Academy, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel, Left Vice Minister of Personnel, and concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
